text:
Predicates:
BredBack(x) ::: x is bred-back.
Resemble(x, y) ::: x resembles y.
Extinct(x) ::: x is extinct.
Animal(x) ::: x is an animal.
ArtificiallySelected(x) ::: x is artificially selected.
Premises:
∀x (BredBack(x) → ArtificiallySelected(x)) ::: Breeding back is a form of artificial selection by the deliberate selective breeding of domestic animals.
BredBack(heckCattle) ∧ Resemble(heckCattle, aurochs) ::: Heck cattle were bred-back in the 1920s to resemble the aurochs.
Animal(heckCattle) ::: Heck cattle are animals.
Animal(aurochs) ::: Aurochs are animals.
∃x ∃y (BredBack(x) ∧ Resemble(x, y) ∧ Extinct(y)) ::: Some animals to be bred-back resemble animals that are extinct.
Conclusion:
∃x (x = heckCattle ∧ ArtificiallySelected(x)) ::: Some Heck cattle are artificially selected.
